name: Znect CI Bridge
description: Experimental read-only CircleCI bridge with MCP tools, browser API, and signed webhook event inbox.

tested: GitHub Actions Ubuntu: TypeScript typecheck and Wrangler dry-run

permissions: Network access to the configured Cloudflare Worker and approved CircleCI API endpoints
Read-only CircleCI project/build data using a secret token
Separate Bearer authentication tokens for MCP and browser JSON API access
dependencies: CircleCI API v3 (current), with legacy API v1.1 compatibility tools
security_controls: Bearer authentication for /mcp with fixed-length digest comparison
Streamable HTTP Origin validation delegated to Cloudflare Agents SDK v2; rejects malformed, opaque, and untrusted browser origins
Fixed CircleCI project path and read-only GET requests
CircleCI redirect rejection and 15-second outbound request timeouts; artifact redirects are manually revalidated
HTTPS artifact URL allowlist and default-port restriction
Streaming log body byte ceiling
Per-action and aggregate log output character limits
Configured Worker secrets redacted from returned logs
Secrets supplied through Cloudflare Worker Secrets
CircleCI API JSON response body size ceiling
Nested workflow/job inspection and automatic diagnostics have explicit page, failed-job, log-action, and artifact budgets to remain below the 50-subrequest Workers Free ceiling
Maximum three allowlisted artifact redirects
Fail-closed HTTP 503 when rate limiting is missing or unavailable
Best-effort pattern redaction for common Bearer/Basic, GitHub/GitLab/Slack, Stripe, Google, npm, AWS, JWT, PEM, and key/value credential formats
Separate Bearer authentication for /mcp (MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN) and /api/v1/* (WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN)
Cloudflare Rate Limiting binding: 60 authenticated MCP and browser API requests per 60 seconds per Cloudflare location
Authenticated rate-limit keys are SHA-256 digests of their respective access tokens; raw tokens are not used as keys
Failed MCP and browser API authentication attempts use a separate SHA-256 client-IP digest bucket
CircleCI outbound webhook ingress verifies v1 HMAC-SHA256 signatures against the exact raw request body
Webhook payloads are capped at 64 KiB, filtered to the fixed Forge project, normalized to allowlisted fields, and deduplicated by CircleCI event ID
SQLite-backed Durable Object stores at most 500 normalized events and prunes events older than 30 days
limitations: Production Cloudflare deployment and end-to-end production MCP behavior are not verified; the current feature-branch head has passed an isolated Cloudflare Preview deployment and authenticated smoke test.

CircleCI API v3 project resolution and read-only access to the fixed Forge project were verified by the authenticated Preview smoke test; broader live run/job/log/artifact response coverage remains to be verified.
Configured Worker secrets and common credential formats are redacted heuristically; custom or encoded upstream secrets may still appear in logs
Wrangler/workerd unsupported in the current Android ARM64 Termux environment
Cloudflare built-in rate limiting is approximate and per location, not a strict global limit; dedicated edge WAF hardening remains advisable.
Rate-limit namespace ID must be unique within the user's Cloudflare account
Heuristic log-secret redaction cannot guarantee detection of all custom or encoded credentials

Webhook ingestion and the durable event inbox passed authenticated synthetic signed-webhook, duplicate-delivery, durable-storage, browser API, and MCP retrieval checks in isolated Preview; registration of a real CircleCI project webhook and real delivery verification remain pending.

Event inbox is queryable through MCP and browser API but does not push unsolicited messages into an open ChatGPT conversation; a supported notification delivery or polling channel remains to be implemented
